neighbours.label: a dash or line break that interrupts a sentence in narrative or reflective prose so that the clause continues after it, as against the same passage with the break replaced by a comma or a full stop
fire: We had planned the trip for months. I kept telling myself it would be fine, that I was, I don't know–ready for whatever came next.
She looked at the old house for a long time. It was smaller than she remembered—smaller and quieter, and somehow sadder.
He opened the letter slowly. Inside was a single photograph of the lake, the cabin, and him—younger, thinner, smiling.
I tried to explain it to my mother. It wasn't that I disliked the job, it was more that I felt, well–trapped by it.
The storm came in fast that evening. We barely had time to close the shutters—and then the power went out.
They walked along the river in silence. Neither of them wanted to say it—that this was the last time.
My grandfather rarely spoke about the war. When he did, his voice changed–lower, slower, almost a whisper.
The kitchen smelled of bread and coffee. For a moment everything felt right—warm, familiar, safe.
